mainEntity.name: Do I need a plug adapter for Europe?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, you will typically need a Type C or Type E/F plug adapter for most of Europe, or a Type G for the UK.

mainEntity.name: Is cash still required in European cities?

acceptedAnswer.text: While cards are widely accepted, it's always good to carry some euros or local currency for small vendors, tips, and public transport.

mainEntity.name: What is the best footwear for cobblestones?

acceptedAnswer.text: Comfortable, thick-soled walking shoes or sturdy sneakers are highly recommended to navigate uneven cobblestone streets safely.

mainEntity.name: Do I need a plug adapter for Japan?

acceptedAnswer.text: Japan uses Type A (two flat pins, same as North America) but usually ungrounded. Make sure your plugs don't have a third grounding pin or bring an adapter.

mainEntity.name: Is cash still required in Japanese cities?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, cash (Yen) is still very heavily used in Japan, especially at smaller restaurants, shrines, and markets.

mainEntity.name: What is the best footwear for temple visits?

acceptedAnswer.text: Slip-on shoes are ideal since you must remove your shoes frequently when entering temples, traditional restaurants, and ryokans.
